correctness.rationale: Every edge pair of K_n intersects in at most one vertex, yielding exactly J/2[sum_v (2k_v-(n-1))^2-n(n-1)] for a plus-edge graph with m edges. An edge-switching proof shows that any vertex-degree gap >=2 can be reduced while keeping m and strictly lowering the squared-degree sum. Hence all and only near-regular degrees realize the fixed-m optimum, for all 0<=m<=N. Direct exact subtraction of the resulting E_n(m) shows a nondecreasing slope sequence, with odd-n even-q rollover values; its distinct half-slopes give the complete critical set. The zero-field parity sectors follow from integer squares and the handshaking parity constraint. Actual standalone checks agree for 33864 small-spin configurations, n=3..100 slope identities, and 2622 graph constructions. No finite experiment was used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The all-field n-parametrized ground-state phase diagram is a natural exact missing invariant for a previously studied complete-root line-graph antiferromagnet, rather than an arbitrary small finite graph computation. Its exact parity-dependent count of distinct magnetic thresholds, the complete simultaneous realizability/characterization of minimizing configurations, and n-even zero-field magnetization sector multiplicity quantify finite-valence frustration invisible to the source's low-temperature mean-field picture. Because the spin count scales quadratically, the finite-size jump is not portrayed as macroscopic density breaking. Potential future use lies in exact zero-temperature benchmarks for graph-based spin systems, not unsupported experimental predictions.
